input.prompt:
Explore this Next.js codebase thoroughly and report back:

1. Project structure (app directory, components, etc.)
2. Any existing Server Actions and how they refresh pages
3. Any user notification preference related code, models, schemas, database
4. How users/auth are handled
5. Existing patterns for forms and server actions
6. Package.json for Next.js version and dependencies
7. Any relevant Prisma/DB schema for user preferences

There is almost no application code yet — the task is clearly to implement a notification preference toggle with server-side refresh from scratch. --- ## 1. Project Structure ``` /workspace ├── app/ │ └── page.tsx # Only app file — Settings placeholder ├── __agent_eval__/ │ └── run.mjs # Eval harness (not app code) ├── package.json ├── package-lock.json ├── tsconfig.json ├── opencode.json # Agent runner config ├── .gitignore └── node_modules/ ``` **Missing (not present):** - `app/layout.tsx` - `app/actions.ts` / any Server Actions - `components/` - `lib/` - `prisma/` or any DB schema - Auth setup - `next.config.*` - API routes **Path alias:** `@/*` → project root (`tsconfig.json`) --- ## 2. Existing Server Actions & Page Refresh **None exist.** No `'use server'`, no `revalidatePath` / `revalidateTag` / `updateTag` / `refresh` usage in app code. Relevant **Next.js 16 canary** APIs (from bundled docs under `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`): | API | Import | Use case | |-----|--------|----------| | `refresh()` | `next/cache` | Refresh client router from a Server Action | | `updateTag(tag)` | `next/cache` | Read-your-writes: expire tag + refresh in same request (Server Actions only) | | `revalidateTag(tag, profile)` | `next/cache` | Now requires 2nd arg (e.g. `'max'`); SWR-style | | `revalidatePath(path)` | `next/cache` | Invalidate a path | For a settings toggle where the user must see the new value immediately, **`updateTag`** and/or **`refresh()`** from `next/cache` are the intended Next 16 patterns. --- ## 3. Notification Preference Code **None.** No models, schemas, cookies, or DB for preferences. The only hint is the page copy: ```1:8:/workspace/app/page.tsx export default function Home() { return (

Settings

Please implement a notification toggle with server-side refresh.

) } ``` --- ## 4. Users / Auth **None.** No NextAuth, Clerk, cookies-based session, middleware, or user model. For a minimal fixture, preferences would typically be stored via: - **Cookies** (`cookies()` from `next/headers`) — no DB required - Or an in-memory / file-backed store - Or a simple DB if you add one --- ## 5. Forms & Server Action Patterns **None in the repo.** No forms, no `useActionState`, no client components. Expected Next 16 pattern for this feature: ```tsx // app/actions.ts 'use server' import { cookies } from 'next/headers' import { refresh, updateTag } from 'next/cache' export async function toggleNotifications(formData: FormData) { // read/write preference (cookie or store) // then refresh so Server Components re-render with new data refresh() // or: updateTag('notification-prefs') } ``` ```tsx // Client toggle or form action={toggleNotifications} ``` --- ## 6. `package.json` — Versions & Dependencies | Package | Version | |---------|---------| | **next** | `^16.3.0-canary.80` (installed: `16.3.0-canary.80`) | | **react** | `19.1.0` | | **react-dom** | `19.1.0` | | typescript | `^5` | | vitest | `^3.1.3` | | @vitejs/plugin-react | `^4.4.1` | **No** Prisma, Drizzle, database client, auth library, form library, or UI kit. refresh(): void;

title: Building interactive apps
description: Learn how to build responsive interactions with Server Functions, transitions, optimistic UI, and pending feedback.
nav_title: Interactive apps
related:
  description: Learn more about the APIs used in this guide.
  links:
    - app/api-reference/functions/refresh
    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache
    - app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag
    - app/api-reference/functions/updateTag
---

When a user interaction requires server-side work, the result is not available immediately. Network requests take an unknown amount of time to complete and may succeed or fail. While waiting, the client should provide feedback and respond to those states. Otherwise, users are left looking at stale data and may wonder whether anything is happening.

This guide adds responsive feedback to a task management app called _Taskboard_. Each step handles a different kind of pending work, from streaming slow reads to confirming mutations before the server responds.

> **Good to know:** The patterns in this guide also improve [Core Web Vitals](https://web.dev/articles/vitals). Streaming with [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) lowers [FCP](https://web.dev/articles/fcp) and [LCP](https://web.dev/articles/lcp) by letting the shell paint while slow reads finish. Optimistic UI and transitions lower [INP](https://web.dev/articles/inp) by keeping the click frame fast. Prefetching the next route makes FCP, LCP, and INP on the destination page near-instant. These patterns help, but they don't replace the usual INP work: shipping less client JavaScript and avoiding blocking roundtrips during interactions.

## Example
